entries.title: Psalms 75:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 The prophet praises God. 2 He promises to judge uprightly. 4 He rebukes the proud by consideration of God's providence. 9 He praises God, and promises to execute justice.

A.M. 3294. B.C. 710. (Title.) Al-tas-chith. or, Destroynot. 57:1; 58:1; *titles A Psalm.Some consider this Psalm to have been written by David on his accession to the throne over all Israel; others refer it to the time of the captivity, considering it as a continuation of the subject in the preceding; but Bp. Patrick and others are of opinion that it was composed by Asaph to commemorate the overthrow of Sennacherib's army, 2 Ki 19:1.

of Asaph. or, for Asaph. for that. 76:1; 138:2; Ex 23:21; 34:6,7; Jer 10:6 wondrous. De 4:7,33,34

entries.title: Psalms 75:2
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: When. 78:70-72; 101:2; 2Sa 2:4; 5:3; 8:15; 23:3,4 receive the congregation. or, take a set time. Ec 3:17; Joh 7:6; Ac 1:7; 17:31

entries.title: Psalms 75:8
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
For in. 11:6; 60:3; Job 21:20; Isa 51:17,22; Jer 25:15,17,27,28 Re 14:9,10; 16:19 it is full.Alluding to the medicated wine or potion of stupifying drugs given to criminals to drink previous to their execution.

Pr 23:30; Isa 5:22 but the dregs. 73:10
